class.name: PIDController
class.brief_description: Proportional-integral-derivative controller for driving a value toward a target with a force.
class.description:
PIDController computes a correction from the error between a measured value and a target. It is useful when you control a value indirectly, through a force, torque or throttle: hovering vehicles, turret aim, steering, temperature or stamina systems. [codeblock] var pid := PIDController.new() pid.proportional_gain = 8.0 pid.integral_gain = 0.5 pid.derivative_gain = 2.0 pid.output_limit = 50.0
func _physics_process(delta): var force := pid.step(global_position.y, hover_height, delta) apply_central_force(Vector3.UP * force) [/codeblock] The derivative term uses the change of the measured value rather than the error, so changing the target does not cause a sudden spike in output.

method.name: get_integral
method.description: Returns the accumulated integral of the error.

method.name: reset
method.description: Clears the accumulated integral and the previous measurement.

method.name: step
method.description: Returns the controller output for the measured [param current] value and the desired [param target] after [param delta] seconds.

members.member: Gain applied to the rate of change of the measured value. Dampens overshoot.
Gain applied to the accumulated error. Removes steady-state error, such as a hovering object sagging under gravity.
If greater than [code]0.0[/code], the accumulated integral is clamped to this magnitude to prevent wind-up.
If greater than [code]0.0[/code], the output is clamped to this magnitude.
Gain applied to the current error.
